utterances.text: But to follow your -- to borrow your term, it's still the judge's call, isn't it? It's up to the judge to decide whether to release the accused or suspect or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. If nothing arrives from the prosecutor, the judge is duty-bound to release that person because there is no obvious need to remand them in custody. On the other hand, even if the proposal arrives from the Prosecutor to release the person, the judge can still turn that proposal down and continue to keep that person in detention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic. Just a second. Yes, Ms. Pelic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, Article 191 can be found under P06178.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dobrijevic, on page 45 -- no. Somewhat earlier. No, no, line 13. You said according to the legislation that is currently in effect, the answer would be yes, and so on and so forth. Because the prosecutor is in charge of the investigation. Can you tell us what has changed in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. The law has been changed. Formerly it was the investigating judge who was in charge of the investigation, in keeping with the Law on Criminal Proceedings, and that was in effect until 2003. It was the investigating judge who decided on remanding people in custody, although the prosecutor could object. It was the judge's call to release people. This is a different law. I apologise. I was talking about the Law on Criminal Procedure that has been in effect since 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would like to deal with your identity. You are not from Dusenovic, are you? And your nickname is Mima?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, my nickname is Mima, however, I was born in the village of Suhaca. I was born on the border between Suhaca, Kamengrad and Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to call up 65 ter 22128 now. This is Mirzet Karabeg's statement. He was a witness here. I'd like to look at page 3 in Serbian and I believe that we need the same page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the second half, Redzo Kurbegovic is mentioned, as well as Ismet Jakupovic. They were interrogated. And it says here Redzo Kurbegovic, Haso Osmancevic, Ismet Alagic, in the cell number 1, Fikret Saletovic, president of the municipal court and so on and so forth. On that day, he was released. However, on the following day, he was brought back in and the interrogation started on the following day. I apologise to the interpreters. It -- the person who interrogated them was a person called Dusenovic whose nickname was Mima. Is that you?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was not me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it shed a new light on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm not sure we have that document before us. Could you locate where it is?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just bear with me for a moment. In Serbian it is page 3. Let me check the English version. Let's go one page back in English. I believe that we will find that paragraph there. No, no, no. Can we go one page forward or, rather, two pages forward from here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Suad Sabic and so on and so forth. This will be in the first third. [In English] The next day, questioning began, questioning was carried out by Dusenovic also known as Mima from Dusenovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was his first name? Mr. Dobrijevic, what was this inspector's first name?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What inspector?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This man Dusenovic whose nickname was Mima?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My chief?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He was your chief?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What was his first name?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mile.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we look at 1D00014?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber who Uros Pena is, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was my colleague and he used to be a policeman. He was the chief of the public security station in Drvar, and then for a while he was the deputy minister. And I believe that for a while he was the chief of the Security Services Centre in Banja Luka or perhaps deputy chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I didn't say that the date of the former document is 13 September 1994. And now look at this document on the screen. It bears the date 19 September 1994. And it says here: "Based on the dispatch that we received from you in connection with information about the activity of the Manjaca camp inmates association in Germany whose president is Adil Draganovic from Sanski Most, we have identified a person named Mile and conducted an interview with him and his father-in-law, Hasim." And it also says here that the person in question is Mile Antonic from Ribnik, and so on and so forth. So it was neither Mile Dusenovic nor Mile Dobrijevic; right?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. A lot of lies can be found in the statements that I've been shown here. There are a lot of lies indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'd like to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, I think -- in the documents shown by Ms. Pelic, I think we saw several Miles already.

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Karabeg said that Dusenovic Mima, Mile, was the one who conducted the interview. His nickname was not Mima but it is Mile. And for some reason, Uros Pena, one week after that statement, sought clarification as to who Mile was and they identified that person as being Mile Antonic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: None of the documents shown to the witness by Ms. Pelic were tendered into evidence. Now you are tendering this official note. For the Chamber to assess all the evidence, we need to accept all the documents shown by the witness -- shown by the Prosecution. If you are tendering this, we have to consider that option as well. Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I don't think it's necessary to tender this under the circumstances. It should bear the same status as the other documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I remember you on this at one point in time, Ms. Pelic. Do you have any observation?

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. Shall we continue?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. If that is in the transcript, then this can stay in the transcript as well, and then I withdraw the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dobrijevic, was Adil Draganovic a person without reproach? Was he questioned without any grounds or were there any grounds for him being interrogated?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let me say this again: I did not interview Adil Draganovic. I do happen to know Adil Draganovic very well. He was the president of the court and he frequently went for on-site investigations with us, and we cooperated extremely well. Allegedly, the reason why he was detained was that Adil Draganovic did not return a Skorpion that he possessed as a member of the state security forces reserve.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 1D00025, please? 1D25.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the Municipal Prosecutor's Office in Buzim. This is in the federation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What is being submitted here is an indictment against Adil Draganovic, the municipal court judge in Sanski Most, for a number of misdemeanours, abuse of office and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at the following page, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then on the front page, it says here that he paid out various payments, acted illegally in handling money. Is this a usual kind of indictment and is this something that is done in this manner when some illegal matters are established?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. This is an indictment charging the accused for committing violations of abuse of office, and his professional authority.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please tender this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives Exhibit Number D4174, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at P6555, page 28, 29, where the Prosecutor suggested that it says over there that a large number of people were sent to Manjaca without being interviewed first. So can we now see whether that was really so. Ah, I'm sorry, I just need to find the right page now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pelic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: If I could help, that's at page 24 in English, line 8 to 15, and in B/C/S page 17.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the bottom, it says, you are speaking: "Well, it was a large number of people, so most probably they could not all be interviewed. There was no time." Where was this large number of people?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sanski Most.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Not that a large number of people went to Manjaca without being interviewed?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably my answer was most probably in that context.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And you were asked why these people were not processed, who had been questioned and sent to Manjaca. Do you know until when Manjaca operated as a prison for prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was until the -- November. I think it was closed in November.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in this document, that was not tendered, it states that Adil Draganovic was working in Germany for some association. Do you know who shut down Manjaca and was this followed by a suspension of all proceedings?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm not aware of this. This was not part of my duties. So I did not really deal with that part of it. I don't know how it was formed or how it was shut down, this Manjaca camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. And if I were to tell you now that Manjaca was closed down and the vast majority of prisoners were pardoned, would that be an answer to the question of why they were not processed?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, then it's clear to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, that's not a proper question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Well, the question was put why they were not processed and the man said that they were submitted and I just wanted to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, move on --

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if you're asking me what the word "abolicija" means, then I can answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Very well. You mentioned that some prisoners, some fighters that were captured, were captured in these three or four villages around Sanski Most and some of them went to Galaja and started guerrilla fighting. Could you please tell us what Galaja is?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Galaja is a forest between Hrustovo and Vrhpolje settlements. In view of the fact that it has a better military strategic position, it was easier to conduct fighting there. It was easier to fight there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So how long did these guerrilla groups last around the Kljuc and Sanski Most woods?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date. It's hard to know that. They were there for a long time. They were divided into these guerrilla-style groups but they didn't have support from the population because the population had left, so then they tried to break through towards Bihac.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In one of the documents proffered by the Prosecution, it is said that there were investigations into the circumstances of the death of Enes Dervisevic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the number?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this something that was ascribed to some Serb as an illegal killing?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Ms. Pelic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure how this is following from my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This name and case appears in the document that was shown --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: And the interpreter did not understand the last part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second, just a second. Mr. Karadzic, the interpreters didn't interpret your question in full because she couldn't hear the number and the name of certain person. Could you repeat that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In one of the documents the Prosecution submitted, the case is mentioned of Enes Dervisevic in the context of an illegal killing or a homicide by a Serb. So what I wanted was to look at 1D25877, a document by Judge Adil Draganovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we see that document, could you not put a question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What I asked was: Was this, this document, and in general, was this something that was ascribed to a Serb as an illegal killing?

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second -- just a second --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you ask me about that, I don't have any knowledge about that whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pelic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: Again, I'm not sure how is this following from my cross-examination and it's leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But is that case appearing in the document you referred to, Ms. Pelic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then let's upload the document used by the Prosecution, start from there. Shall we take a break?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. But I was actually thinking of completing my questioning by just look -- but we can look at the document that looks at the investigation into the killing of Enes Dervisevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's the number in which that individual appears?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need to find it, Your Excellencies, it was shown by the Prosecution so I really -- I just need to find it. Perhaps it would be better to go on the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We will have a break for 45 minutes and resume at 1.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, your Excellency. I'm going to cut things short a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I wanted to ask you this: You were asked about the confiscation of weapons of non-Serbs. Did you confiscate illegal weapons from non-Serbs as well?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all illegal weapons were confiscated. Also, we tried to process the merchants of illegal weapons because this is a criminal offence. It constitutes a criminal offence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And was this a permanently confiscated or not, and who makes that decision?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We confiscate the weapons on a temporary basis, we issue a certificate, and the court is the one who decides whether the weapon will be permanently confiscated.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. I would need to ask you for a favour, for somebody to put a document on the ELMO because I didn't know that this would come up.

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we please see the document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: There are ERN numbers. All are official.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you able to tell the Trial Chamber what this document is and from whom are the documents being confiscated?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a certificate on the temporary confiscation of an item from Budinka Svetlitca [phoen]. An automatic M56 weapon is being confiscated, factory number E69353, with one round and 25 bullets, and it's a calibre 7.62.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what is Budinka? Can we look at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pelic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, this is related to 1994 and I'm just wondering how it's relevant to my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can I hear from you, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Throughout the war the policy was the same, in terms of illegal arming. This is something that the witness is aware of. This is not something that applied only to 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But confiscation has nothing to do with the cross-examination. Please move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President I think it shows that they were treating Serbs equally as they were treating Muslims because during the cross-examination there was issues regarding the treatment of Muslims in Sanski Most and the lack of enforcement against Serbs who were committing crimes against Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pelic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I was focusing on 1992 and this is 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would you like to add anything with respect to the time frame, Mr. Robinson?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, if Dr. Karadzic an elicits from the witness that they were doing the same thing during 1994 as they had been doing in 1992 it would be relevant. Otherwise, it wouldn't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the next one, please? [In English] Just to see the seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the same kind of document? [In English] Confiscation is disarmament --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, this is 95 again, yes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Or 94, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: I would like to see the seal down there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber said you should move on, not allowing this line of question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: But, Mr. President, do you remember we had the issue about what the seal looked like for Sanski Most and the other document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, very well, on that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dobrijevic, does this look like the stamp of your station?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It can clearly be seen here the public security station of Sanski Most. It can clearly be read. It's in the Cyrillic script.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is for that purpose that I would like to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It receives MFI D4175, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Last question: You said that you guarded villages that did not express readiness to fight. How did the situation on the front line affect the safety of Muslims --

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour, this again has nothing to do with my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I beg your pardon?

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: It's not raising from the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your point is not you are -- Mr. Karadzic is not properly citing his evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: I didn't cross-examine Mr. Dobrijevic on guarding of villages that did not express readiness to fight.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But -- but three villages, Hrustovo, Vrhpolje, and I don't know which one, were represented as the entire municipality where there was fighting, and the witness said that it was only those three villages that were involved in fighting. They were guarding the rest because they had handed over their weapons. So it has to do with that, the attitude towards the villages and towards the non-Serbs.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think I follow your explanation. Move on to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if it's another topic, then I have no further questions, but the problem is how I understand this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, can we hear you on that, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Actually, I'm not understanding how Dr. Karadzic is linking this. I recall his direct examination covering these topics, but I'm not sure how he's linking this to the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you very much, indeed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: If I may clarify further, I understand that I may be confused because I am an amateur, but during the cross-examination it was alleged that villages have been disarmed and then attacked, and I want to see whether those villages have been attacked or guarded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you are referring to a document which refers to disarming in quotation marks, so peaceful disarming and attack?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then we'll hear your question. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please tell us who could have attacked the villages or who was it that did attack the villages, the villages that were you guarding? You were protecting them from who?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were guarding the local population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Pelic. It's difficult to see you from here. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's again a leading question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, when it was suggested that the villages had been disarmed, under quotation marks, and then attacked, did that actually happen and who was it that could have attacked the villages?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the question is a bit unclear to me but let me try to answer. Everybody could have attacked, Serbs, non-Serbs. Most of the crimes that were committed after combat operations or rather after a voluntary surrender of weapons, were properly -- property-related; that is to say robbery, armed robbery, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In that context, could the village have been attacked by someone who was affected by combat operations from Bihac, et cetera? Did you have a problem like that?

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: Again, leading.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Could you have -- could you reformulate your question, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Dobrijevic, was it your understanding that it was only regular military and police forces that could have attacked the villages? Or was there somebody else?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no danger coming from the legitimate police force. It was the duty and responsibility of the police to guard them, to protect them. I've already said there was the danger of certain groups that stayed on and that were moving from Bihac, Galaja, Prijedor, and so on. These were some of the routes that they took on their way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the MUP take all of that into account?

utterances.speaker: MILE DOBRIJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the last document please be shown to the witness on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please read out the entire document, read it out loud.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could it be shown to the Prosecutor first?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: It was. It had been shown in the batch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. Yes, Ms. Pelic?

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Oh, that was your point. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PELIC
utterances.text: One more point. It's again related to 1994 and my cross-examination was specifically directed to 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My position is that a phenomenon is a phenomenon. It cannot be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could the witness read out the title of this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ministry of the Interior, Republika Srpska, dispatch, CJB Prijedor, SJB Sanski Most. The dispatch is sent from the SJB Sanski Most to Prijedor which is within Prijedor. It is connected to dispatch SJB Sanski Most number 11-19-1, 91/94, from the 21st of December 1994. In view of the existing war situation and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic? Before putting that question, let us know first.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Well, I did pose this question just a minute ago, whether police took everything in account in order to prevent any attack on the villages, contrary to the allegations that villages have been attacked by official forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think this is relevant to the issue that we discussed here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please move on to another topic. We'll not allow this question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. Thank you, Mr. Dobrijevic, I have no further questions. Unfortunately, there are far more documents but I don't have all that time. But any way, thank you very much for having come.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Well, that concludes your evidence, Mr. Dobrijevic. On behalf of the Chamber, I'd like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. Now you are free to go.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour, for this possibility to say what I had, and thank you for your fairness. Thank you once again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. May I just raise one matter before the next witness comes in which is related to a motion from the Defence which you have or will shortly receive. It was filed at some point in the last session. It's a notice of testimony and request for presence of counsel related to Mr. Beara, which is also related to the similar motion filed in connection with Mr. Tolimir. I simply wanted to alert the Court to the fact that these two motions are part of an ongoing collaborative dialogue between the Defence and the Prosecution aimed at ensuring the most efficient use of court time, particularly in the face of many, many scheduling changes that have arisen by the Defence and that have put a significant strain on Prosecution resources in attempting to deal with. We've done our best to -- and continue to do our best to ensure that to the maximum extent possible the court schedule can move forward with minimal and thus far actually almost none existent disruption, but I wanted to note that these two motions arise from our exchange and reflect the Defence's recognition of the strain and difficulties that these many, many changes put on the Prosecution resources, and it's an attempt to avoid yet a further and quite unnecessary additional expenditure of resources and difficulty for the Prosecution, under these circumstances, where in fact we don't know and even have indications that the witnesses will not testify. So the schedule proposed by Mr. Robinson, which of course I'm indicating we strongly endorse, is that these two witnesses would appear at the latter part of that week, would, if they chose to do so, proffer their evidence-in-chief, and then their cross-examination would be deferred until after the break. So I think that's eminently sensible under the circumstances. It works out well with the schedule as the Court can see, it avoids the unnecessary further strain on Prosecution resources, and so we -- we ask the Court to adopt that approach as suggested by Mr. Robinson and agreed upon by us. I would note that indeed, if -- given the adjustments we've already been obliged to make, we would not be prepared to cross-examine without -- at least not in the absence of imposing a really draconian and unfair schedule on the lawyer or lawyers involved. So we ask the Court to follow the proposal of the parties in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, would you like to add anything?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Only, Mr. President, that we have been receiving excellent cooperation from the Prosecution in adjusting to our changes in the witness lineup, and we think that this is a reasonable solution to continue the flow of witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Has that been discussed with the witness in question?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, the witness -- it's been discussed with -- the witness's counsel is aware of it, but we don't have any --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I mean the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's been duly noted and the Chamber will consider the matter in due course. Before we bring in the next witness, there are four matters I'd like to deal with briefly. First, in relation to the Chamber's order on the 4th of December to lift the confidentiality of a portion of the transcript. The Chamber hereby instructs the Registry that pages 44417, line 10, to 44419, line 4, of the transcript of 3rd of December 2013, as well as the relevant portion of the audiovisual recording, can now be made available to the public. Second, on the 5th December 2013, the accused filed a notice of questions for General Tolimir and request for presence of legal adviser. On the same day, the Prosecution informed the Chamber via e-mail that it did not wish to respond to this filing. The Chamber takes no issue with Zdravko Tolimir's legal adviser, Mr. Aleksandar Gajic, being present in the courtroom during Tolimir's testimony. This request is therefore granted. Third, the Chamber now wishes to issue an oral ruling in relation to Witness Milos Milincic, who is scheduled to testify next week. The Rule 92 ter notification for this witness was filed on the 29th of November 2013. His proposed Rule 92 ter statement bears 65 ter number 1D9746. Having reviewed the proposed evidence of this witness, the Chamber is concerned about its lack of relevance to the charges laid against the accused. This is particularly pertinent when regard is had to the claim of the accused that he is pressed for time. There are very few paragraphs of potential general relevance to the indictment in the proposed Rule 92 ter statement, namely parts of paragraphs 9, 10, 16, 18, 19, 20, and 22. The remainder of the statement is purely about the situation in Srbac, a municipality which is not included in the indictment, the policies developed there and the impact of the conflict in the neighbouring Croatia. Accordingly, Milincic will not be allowed to be called pursuant to Rule 92 ter. If the accused wishes to call him on matters relevant to the indictment, he can do so viva voce. Finally, as the Defence case is drawing to a close, the Chamber would benefit from hearing from the parties and stand-by counsel as to whether stand-by counsel should continue to perform the duties to which he was assigned after the close of the Defence case or of rebuttal and rejoinder, if any, and until the completion of the closing arguments. The Chamber therefore requests the parties and Mr. Harvey to file their written submission on this topic no later than Friday, 13th of December 2013. That said, shall we bring in the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, while we are bringing in this witness, we have 45 minutes of cross-examination and maybe 15 minutes of direct, is it possible to make arrangements to sit until maybe 3.30 today since we started late so that we can conclude his evidence today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will ask around and see how it evolves.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Would the witness make the solemn declaration, please. Mr. Bojinovic, do you hear me in a language you understand? Can you -- shall we turn up the volume for the witness? Now do you hear me in your language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Bojinovic. Would you make the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Bojinovic. Please be seated and make yourself comfortable. Before you commence your evidence, Mr. Bojinovic, I must draw your attention to a certain rule of evidence -- yes. If the usher could assist the witness. Now, do you hear me well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Okay. I wanted to draw your attention to a rule of evidence that we have here at the International Tribunal, that is Rule 90(E). Under this rule, Mr. Bojinovic, you may object to answering any question from Mr. Karadzic, the Prosecutor, or even from the Judges if you believe that your answer might incriminate you in a criminal offence. In this context, "Incriminate" means saying something that might amount to an admission of guilt for a criminal offence or saying something that might provide evidence that you might have committed a criminal offence. However, should you think that an answer might incriminate you and as a consequence you refuse to answer the question, I must let you know that the Tribunal has the power to compel you to answer the question. But in that situation, the Tribunal would ensure that your testimony, compelled under such circumstances, would not be used in any case that might be laid against you for any offence, save and except the offence of giving false testimony. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Good day, Mr. Bojinovic.

utterances.speaker: MILOS BOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Good day, good day, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please let us pause between my questions and your answers and also let us enunciate our sentences slowly so that they could be recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MILOS BOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bojinovic, did you testify before this Tribunal, and if so in which case?

utterances.speaker: MILOS BOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the Brdjanin case ten years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have 1D9730 in e-court? And also could 9730A be prepared?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether you had an opportunity to be reminded of that testimony of yours? Did you manage to listen to it or to read through it?

utterances.speaker: MILOS BOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Part of it. I reviewed part of it, but I remember the trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This transcript, did it faithfully reflect what you said at that trial during your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MILOS BOJINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Everything is fine, all of what I reviewed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are there some parts which was asked in private session or in closed session?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. We are going to be tendering 1D9730 under seal and 1D9730A as a public document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. So as long as this page is concerned, it was conducted in open session?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, and it's actually not necessary to upload the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no. There is no signature on it. Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If I were to put the same questions to you today, the questions that were put during that testimony of yours, would your answers basically be the same?

utterances.speaker: MILOS BOJINOVIC
utterances.text: I think they would be.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, I would like to tender that exhibit according to Rule 92 ter, the redacted version and the full version, according to the numbers that we referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Bojinovic, to the question of Mr. Karadzic that whether you listened to the audio video tape of your testimony or read this transcript, and you said part of it. I reviewed part of it but I remember the trial. And then --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you meant? I take it you do not read English, Mr. Bojinovic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Well, I reviewed one part of the CD and I could see that everything was all right. I did not look at the second part of the CD because it could not be activated. This is what I meant. And I believe that the second part of the CD has to be all right if the first part was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How long did it take for you to review the first part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, to be honest, about an hour. I can't give you the precise time. I didn't time it. But that would be my estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, can you assist us here, please? Now, he's saying I believe the second part of the CD has to be right because the first part was. Now, would that be confirmation of the second part?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, I think in -- under these circumstances, he's saying that he recalls his testimony in Brdjanin and that it was accurate, and we did -- I'm hearing actually for the first time that he didn't complete the listening to the CD because we brought that CD to him to listen to his testimony before he testified, but I think that if he believes that what he has listened to so far is consistent with his recollection and that the testimony in that case was accurate and he would repeat the same here, I think that that's sufficient under 92 ter. But I apologise for the fact that he wasn't able to listen to his entire testimony, which should have been done. But if it's of concern to the Chamber, we can have him listen to it over the weekend and he can give his testimony on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Ms. Sutherland, can you assist us in this matter? You wish to respond at all?

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: It was going to be my submission on hearing what the witness said, that I don't believe the requirements of Rule 92 ter have been met. He said that he listened to one hour of audio. He testified over two days and it was I think half an hour short of the end of the session on the second day that his evidence was completed. So he's only listened to one hour of seven, approximately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Yes, he said the second part of the CD couldn't have been activated or words to that effect.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, that's what he said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: -- which means that hasn't --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: I presume the second part of the CD means the second day, but even in fact he hasn't, as I can work it out, reviewed the whole of day 1 even. And I think the better course may be that he listens to the entirety of his evidence over the weekend so that he can be sure that -- that it accurately reflects what he would say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Bojinovic, would there be any problem if you have to stay till Monday next week?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it would be a problem. May I explain? I have reviewed the first day of that trial, and everything was accurate. In my view any delay would be unnecessary, especially for the reason being that I didn't review the second day. I don't think that there is anything inaccurate there. If there were inaccuracies, I would certainly alert you to those, but I don't think that there are. I'm absolutely sure that we can continue my testimony without any delays. I would have a problem if I had to stay because I have a lot of commitments in my place of residence, at the grammar school, at the high school, I have a lot of commitments, and on top of that my health is not all that good. That's why I would like to suggest that we should continue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber is of the view that requirements for the admission of his statement -- transcript pursuant to Rule 92 ter is not met. The Chamber is very much concerned about this situation, and if similar situation happens in the future, the Chamber may consider taking the lost time to the Defence time, taking out from the Defence time allotted. But in the circumstances, I will leave to the Defence whether to lead this witness live now or postpone his evidence to tomorrow -- to Monday at 9.00 or reschedule his evidence in a proper manner, given the witness's circumstances.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour, we won't lead his evidence live because we wouldn't finish his testimony today in any event, so we will discuss with the witness and either he'll testify on Monday or he'll come back at another time or we will make a motion under 92 bis to admit his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Unless there is any other matters to be dealt with or raised --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will resume on Monday at 9.00. The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 9th day of December, 2013, at 9.00 a.m. 24 25
